notes: The Grid Console pair has the line-art tracks, nodes and timetable margins the owner called high style, carried through Home, Ideas, To do, Status and Plans. It keeps a real halo on the question, the key word and the gauge, with grounded blues, ambers and violets elsewhere. Keyed edges ahead because it improves the To do controls. Desk Terminal is the most machine-like, with the CRT on every page's side monitor, but its trays are heavier and its rails less drawn. Lit Index has the best typesetting and the ledger is a lovely idea, but the giant lit headline risks the glare the owner wants calmed, and the page leans editorial away from the terminal.

scores.why: Bright green everywhere, near-monochrome (83% green), flat dark cards; the glow DNA is there but the page is the baseline the owner found too bright and too samey.

Signal Box's line language (rails, lamps, a NOW node, a timetable margin on To do) runs through every page. It adds a grounded cool palette, a real glow on the question and the gauge, and a calm lattice. The green Add key and latched pills make To do's controls better, and a lit corner marks the first cell. Faint at half size, but this is the closest to what the owner has praised.

Same lattice, rails and glowing key word, grounded and unmistakably CRT on every page. It is just the parent without the To do control improvements: a plain Add fold and a select where a pill row would do.

Slate trays, a thin monitor on every page, a bigger lit question on the glass and numbered rails. Strong CRT soul and orderly. The setup strip first pushes Coming up below the fold, and the even dock is barely visible.

The same Desk Terminal with a smaller question and banded plates. A coherent machine-and-trays system with grounded colour, but a little boxy and less changed from today in feel than the Grid Console.

Editorial poster type with a lit MIND? and a ledger of tick wells, dotted leaders and amber stamps on To do. The typesetting is excellent and the page is clearly different. But the giant glowing headline is glare-prone and the page reads more magazine than CRT terminal, with the glass confined to one monitor.

The same bold editorial type and coloured section rules, with strong typography and the monitor kept. The To do page is a plain list with no rail art, and it is the furthest from the machine feel and line art the owner loves.

fixes.suggestion: Keep the rails, the NOW node, the green key, the pills and the glowing key word. Make the lit corner visible at half size on Status and Plans, and bring the pills to Ideas so both filter pages share one control system.
Keep the lattice and rails. Take the green Add key and the pills from r20-mut-3 for To do. Strengthen the faint section accents slightly.
Keep the thicker glass question and the thin case. Put Finish setting up below Coming up, or collapse it, so the first screen still shows the plans. Make the dock equalising visible, or drop it.
Keep the tray system and the rail numerals. Open the bands as r20-mut-1 does and enlarge the glass question.
Keep the ledger on To do and the type scale. Tone the MIND bloom down a step and show the radar or glass larger on Home. Widen the Home ledger so titles do not wrap.
Keep the poster headlines and the coloured head rules. Add the ledger rail to To do and a thin monitor to the list pages. Soften the large halo.

notes: I judged by how much green-screen life each design has while the rest of the page stays grounded. Desk Terminal puts the light where attention belongs: a typed question on a real tube, a chart, and a dial gauge on Status. The change reaches every page. Lit Index has the loudest single phosphor gesture, the lit MIND with its scanlined bloom, but it is closer to a lit sign than a screen, and the rest of the page is editorial. Grid Console is the calmest and most grounded, and the most generic once you leave the tube. r20-mut-1 is the best of the Desk Terminal line because of the heavier, hotter question. r20-mut-2 edges r19-mut-3 for the lit question mark.

scores.why: The original tube light is real (halo on 'mind', glowing monitors, scanlines) and lively. It is nearly monochrome and the rest of the page is plain cards, so it is the yardstick for soul, not for system.

The most complete green-screen soul. The question is typed on the glass in a hot, heavy monitor face with a LISTENING status line and cursor. The Next up tube plots a chart, and Status gets a real dial gauge on a CRT. The 56px question and the even dock make it better than r19-mut-1. Grounded neutrals and amber stamps sit around the lit parts, and the change shows on every page.

The same terminal-on-the-desk idea, with the same tube chart, gauge and radar. The question is a notch smaller and the dock ends unevenly. It is still one of the clearest phosphor identities in the field, with light kept to the glass.

A huge scanline-barred MIND with a layered halo, and now a lit question mark, is the boldest phosphor moment in the field, and it reads as a lit sign. The tubes stay real, and the cool grounded rail and big condensed heads show across pages. The poster tips toward glare, and the page is more editorial than green-screen below the tube.

Same lit-index poster as r20-mut-2 without the lit question mark, so the light feels slightly unfinished. The grounded colour and type system are strong, but fewer lit green-screen details outside Home's tube.

A calm lattice with a faint lit corner, a green key and latched pills. It reads as a grounded modern console with a green accent. The tube and radar are still real, but the typed question is a grey-white headline and the phosphor shows less across the page.

The grid and the NOW-marker timeline are tidy and the tubes keep their glow. The green is the calmest here, and the light is mostly a lattice and a few tubes, so it has the least tube feeling of the six.

fixes.suggestion: Keep the typed question on the glass, the LISTENING line, the gauge and the chart tube. Fix the order: Coming up drops below the fold when Finish setting up leads. Keep the setup strip thin or move it below the dock. Let the question wrap fully inside the glass at 56px. Give the setup steps one rule, not three dashed cells.
Keep it as the calmer terminal fallback. Take the 56px question and hotter core from r20-mut-1, and the equal-height dock. Otherwise leave it.

Keep the lit MIND and question mark and the cool rail, but cap the bloom so the poster glows rather than glares. Put one real phosphor face below the fold, for example a typed readout on the Vera section, so the soul is not confined to Home's top. Let the ledger titles run a little wider.
Superseded by r20-mut-2. If kept, light the question mark and add a typed readout beside the big heads.
Make the lit corner visible at half size, and move the question onto the glass or give it a typed status line. Give Ideas the same pill controls as To do. Keep the green key.
Keep the NOW marker and its lit line to the dot. Put the question in the monitor face and add scanlines and halo to the grid's primary cell so it has more tube in it.

notes: The two Lit Index designs are the most distinctive: a poster-scale lit question in a condensed grotesque, numbered sections and a CRT inset. They look unlike today on every page and answer the call to bring back the lit effect where attention belongs. r20-mut-2 is the better of the two because its lit question mark and ledger finish the idea. The Desk Terminal pair is the most charming system (an instrument per page) but more conventional in layout. The Grid Console pair has a cohesive spine-and-nodes world and the tournament's best controls (in r20-mut-3), but it risks a dashboard feel. Today's page scores low for being monochrome and generic despite its good glow.

scores.why: The original tube light is the most atmospheric thing here (halo, scanlines, bloom), but the page is one green on black with soft cards, so it reads as a stock dark theme with a glow. The family's 'Matrix' remark still applies.

The boldest and most memorable identity: a huge condensed 'WHAT'S ON YOUR MIND?' lit as one phosphor line, numbered index sections with coloured rules, and a CRT inset. The ledger on To do and the lit question mark fix the parent's loose ends. It looks different from today on every page, and the heavy display type is a strong, tasteful use of typography.

The same Lit Index poster with the same strong type, scale contrast and index numbering. The unlit question mark leaves the line half-lit, and To do is a plain stack of rows without the ledger's charm. Still the second most distinctive page.

A considered 'desk' idea: the question typed on a glass, a docked tube per page (gauge on Status, radar on Ideas, bars on To do) and a contents plate. Charming and coherent, with the bolder 56px question helping. It is a calmer, more conventional two-column layout than the Lit Index, and the even-dock change is nearly invisible.

The wiring-spine and grid-floor world is a quiet personality with lavender, amber and blue nodes. The green 'Add' key and latched pills on To do give it tactile controls, a real gain. It is busy and dashboard-like, and the lit corner is too faint to register.

The same desk terminal with a tube per page, good use of the green on the glass, and calm grounded panels. Its Home gets setup after Coming up, which is fine, but the question is smaller and the page feels like a tidy console rather than an identity.

The same Grid Console world, with the spine, nodes, big gauge and headline numerals in lavender. Nice detail, but it has few controls beyond the parent's, the many coloured rules feel decorative, and it sits close to today's card layout.

fixes.suggestion: Keep the lit poster, the index numbers and the ledger. Bring the ledger to Home at full width so titles do not wrap, move 'Finish setting up' below the question as a quieter strip, and add the Desk Terminal's per-page instrument to Status and Settings so the tube is not only on Home.
Keep the type system and index. Light the question mark as MIND is, and give To do the ledger rows. The unlit gaps between the poster and the lower bands feel empty.

Keep the glass question and the docked instruments. Make the dock-equalising visible or drop it, restore Coming up above the fold by making the setup strip one line, and take the heavier question stroke to the other page titles for rhythm.

Keep the green key and latched pills, and use them on Ideas and Settings too so controls agree. Make the lit corner larger and more present on the primary cell, and calm the grid floor and the number of rule colours.
Keep the tube-per-page docking. Strengthen the question to the 56px treatment and open the bands so they sit on the page like the Lit Index.
Keep the spine and the gauge. Adopt the controls from r20-mut-3 and reduce the number of coloured rules and numerals to one accent per page.

notes: The difference between these six is largely which of three systems they use. Lit Index is a typographic poster with a lit headline, Grid Console is a lattice with a rail, and Desk Terminal is a tube dock. Lit Index changes the page most visibly and most typographically, and recovers the original tube's bloom at the headline without spreading glare. Grid Console has the best controls and the best time-line signalling (the Now marker). Desk Terminal is the calmest, but also the nearest to today. Round 20's refinements help all three: the ledger, the keys and pills, and the even dock. The final standard would be best built from Lit Index's type and light, Grid Console's controls and Now rail, and Desk Terminal's dock for Status pages.

scores.why: Coherent and calm, but near-monochrome cards on black, with uniform rounded panels and little hierarchy or type system. It is the baseline the owner called near-identical across rounds.

The strongest type system of the six: condensed display faces, mono kickers on one 13.6px step, numbered index, tinted rules per page. The lit MIND? poster brings the tube's bloom back exactly where attention belongs. The To do ledger (well, branch, leader, tabular who/when, amber stamp) is a rule that would hold on any list. It changes every page the family sees. Risks are poster-scale headings dominating Settings and a sparse Home wishes column.

A tickless lattice with a rail and lit corner is a consistent structure on Status, Plans, To do and Settings, and the Now timeline on To do is excellent. The green key and latched pills make the controls system visible and 44px. It is a little fussy (many rails and cards), and Ideas still uses selects, so the control system is uneven.

The most comfortable and consistent: one tube dock and contents plate on every page, open bands, a calm ledger. The 56px glass question is a good tube moment. But it is the most incremental over r19-1, and Finish setting up first pushes Coming up below the fold. The look across pages is still close to today's cards-and-sidebar.

Same typographic poster system as r20-2 with the glow on MIND, but To do keeps tall, roomy rows with an unlit question mark. The ledger is the clear improvement, so this is the parent of the better design.
A solid grid and rail system, but the To do and Ideas controls are plain selects and an unkeyed Add fold. It is superseded by r20-3's key, pills and lit corner.
A clean dock system with good dials, but Coming up and the Contents plate end at unequal heights. The setup band sits low, and the plates stay heavy. It is superseded by r20-1's refinements.

fixes.suggestion: Keep the poster question, the lit ?, the ledger and the 13.6px kicker step. Cap Settings and Ideas row titles one step smaller so the heads do not outshout the content. Give Home's ledger a wider who column. Add a pill or key control to Ideas filters, as r20-3 does.

Keep the Now timeline on To do, the green key, the pills and the lit corner. Extend pills to Ideas so the controls are consistent. Thin the rails and cards a step to calm the lattice, and make the lit corner visible at half size.

Keep the 56px glass question, the even dock and the open bands. Put Coming up back above the fold, with setup as a slim strip that does not take a full band. Drop the underline from the setup steps. Add one display face on the page heads to give the type more range.
Take r20-2's ledger and lit question mark. Otherwise it is the parent and holds nothing further.
Take r20-3's key, pills and lit corner. Keep the lattice and the footer lamp. Reduce rail clutter.
Keep the dock and the dial gauge as the system for status pages. Adopt r20-1's equal heights and open bands; otherwise it is superseded.

notes: The three families differ in how fast a glance finds the one action. Lit Index (r20-mut-2) wins: the question is enormous and lit, the Send key follows it directly, and the numbered bands give clear tiers when squinted. It is also the only finalist that clearly brings back the original phosphor glow on words. Grid Console Keyed has the best controls: pills show state, the green key is a real primary action, and Send says Send. Its hierarchy is flatter, since every band is a similar-weight bordered cell. Desk Terminal is the most explanatory, with its status line and Contents plate. It reads closest to today's page, so it risks the owner's "nearly identical" complaint. All finalists beat today's page on comprehension. The ledger To do and the pill row are the clearest list and control ideas.

scores.why: The Home box and radar tube read well, but every band is the same dark card, so the squint shows one grey mass. Controls are clear, with good focus rings. The nav and lists give little sense of what matters first.

Strongest sight line: the huge lit MIND question, then Send, then ways to start, and the squint still reads title then action then bands. The To do ledger (tick, title, leader, who/when, amber stamp) is the quickest list to scan. The 2/62 small targets and the 00-05/A-D tab codes are minor costs.

Best controls of the field: To do's latched 44px pills, a green Add key, and a Send button that says Send. The coloured section rails with the NOW marker and the due timeline make state clear. 0 small targets. The lit corner is too faint to teach anything and Ideas still uses selects, so control language is inconsistent.

The same lit poster and numbered rail as r20-mut-2 with a clear hierarchy, but its To do list is the plainer version and the question mark is dimmer. The glance is good, though the ledger adds scan speed over it.

Calm grid with clear section heads, a timeline to NOW and a tab bar with icons and caps labels. A small Send icon button and a tiny composer make the main action less obvious. The quiet corner ticks add nothing a viewer notices.

The terminal glass with its LISTENING status line and heavier 56px question explains what the machine is doing. The ledger lists with leaders scan well, and the Contents plate helps orientation. Putting setup first pushes Coming up below the fold, and the page stays close to today in feel.

The same Desk Terminal with comprehension aids (Contents plate, ledger rows, big Send). The dock ends unevenly and the question is smaller, so the glance is softer. A real step up from today but the least decisive hierarchy among the finalists.

fixes.suggestion: Keep the lit poster question, the ledger and the staggered thread. Fix the 2 targets under 44px. Replace the 00-05 and A-D tab codes with plain words, or add titles to them, so a first-time visitor knows what they open. Let the ledger take the full width on Home so titles don't wrap.

Keep the pills, the Add key and the Send label. Give Ideas the same pills instead of three selects. Make the lit corner visible at half size or drop it. Bring in some of r20-mut-2's poster scale on the question so the glance has one dominant thing.
Superseded by r20-mut-2; its question mark is dimmer and its To do has no ledger. Carry over the ledger and lit mark.
Make Send a labelled button on the phone and in the desk composer. Make the lit corners visible or remove them. Keep the NOW marker and the timeline.

Keep the LISTENING status on the glass and the bolder question. Put Coming up back ahead of setup once setup is a strip, or collapse setup to one line, so the first screen shows content. Remove the underline under each step so it stops reading as dashed cells.
Keep the Contents plate and ledger rows. Take the bolder question and the equal-height dock from r20-mut-1. Add more contrast between the section bands so the squint reads in tiers.

notes: The Lit Index pair clearly leads on typesetting. They bring a real type scale (poster, page head, section head, body, mono kicker), numbered indexes, big counted figures and tabular ledger columns, all in faces that suit the phosphor feel. r20-mut-2 edges its parent through the lit question mark, the larger kickers and the To do ledger. Grid Console is a close second family, with condensed heads, figures beside titles and a better secondary ink. The Desk Terminal pair keeps today's flat sans hierarchy and spends its effort on the monitor, so it improves the typography least. Today's page is competent but unscaled.

scores.why: Clean DM Sans with a lit key word and mono kickers, but one weight and one scale. Titles, section heads and list rows sit close in size, so the hierarchy is flat and nothing sets a rhythm.

The strongest hierarchy of the six. The condensed display face gives the poster title, the numbered page heads, the big figures and the ledger rows a clear scale. The mono kickers, now 13.6px and tracked, and the tabular columns in the To do ledger are careful typesetting. Lighting the question mark to match MIND makes the poster one lit line, and the chat leader tidies the thread.

Same type system as its child: a condensed display face for titles and heads, a quiet grotesque for body, and mono caps for labels and index numbers. Hierarchy and pairing are excellent. The unlit question mark leaves the poster slightly uneven, and the kickers are a touch small.

Condensed headings with big tabular figures (Ideas 12, Status 6), mono tracked kicker labels and a lifted secondary ink that helps legibility. Pills and the key button give the controls a tidier type treatment. It is more restrained than Lit Index, so the scale is less dramatic.

The same good system as r20-mut-3: condensed heads, figure callouts, small-cap mono labels and the numbered grid index. The secondary ink is dimmer and the kind labels are weaker, so small text is a little less crisp.

The 56px stroked pixel-mono question is a bolder, more legible glass line, and the open bands cut box noise. Below it the page is still a mid-weight sans with small mono tags, so the hierarchy is only modestly better than today's.
The glass question is pixel mono at 44px with a small status line, which is on-motif. The page around it keeps today's flat scale, and the plates and gauges draw the eye more than the type does.

fixes.suggestion: Keep the lit question mark, the 13.6px kickers and the ledger. Widen the Home To do ledger or drop the leader so titles do not wrap to two lines. Check that the lit MIND does not glare on a bright screen, and use old-style or tabular figures consistently for dates.
Keep the display face and the numbered heads. Lift the kicker size and tracking as r20-mut-2 does, and light the question mark so the poster reads as one line.
Keep the lifted secondary ink and the weight-650 kind labels. Extend the pill and key treatment to the Ideas selects so the controls are typeset the same way. Raise the small mono labels a step.
Adopt the lifted secondary ink and the stronger kind labels from r20-mut-3. Keep the tabular figures beside the page titles.

Keep the heavier 56px glass question. Give section heads a real display step, as Lit Index does, so the page below the glass has a hierarchy. Set the setup steps without underline rules so they stop reading as dashed cells.
Add a display step for page and section titles and raise the small mono tags. Use tabular figures in the Coming up and To do columns, and keep the typed glass line.

notes: I judged on cards only. All six candidates keep the bright #6dff9c in the same places, and the family would notice the structural differences across the pages. The ones that help a first-time user are the labelled Send, the visible pills in place of a select, the stamped overdue state, a calendar with marked days, and a NOW marker. Grid Console Keyed adds the most of these and has the best text contrast. Desk Terminal Even Dock is the easiest to read and the most familiar. Lit Index is the most striking but the weakest to use, because of the tiny uppercase mono and the oversized phone headline.

scores.why: Readable and consistent, with a labelled nav and a clear Home box. But the Send button is icon-only, To do is plain cards with no overdue emphasis, Show is a select, and the 17:1 white-on-black is the glare the owner objects to.

Best control clarity. Show is latched pills (Open, Done, Cancelled, All) instead of a select, Add something to do is a green key, and Send says Send on the phone. The To do timeline with a lit NOW marker and due dates shows state at a glance, and the Plans calendar marks days that have plans. It has the best measured text contrast (5.56) and no Home targets under 44px. Costs: tiny mono uppercase labels, and only To do got pills, so Ideas still has selects.

Familiar and effortless. The phone Home has a big labelled Send, a clear From row, the mic, and starter chips. Icon-and-label tabs have an underline on the current one. The To do ledger stamps overdue items in amber ('was due 6 days ago'), and the Contents dock lists what is on each page. Zero small targets. The side tube column costs width on lists.

The same strong base as r20-mut-1: labelled Send, the select shows a check on the chosen item, Show is a button group, and overdue is stamped. Its dock and plate are slightly uneven, and bands still carry plates, so the page is busier.

Clear structure: counts in heads, a To do timeline with a NOW marker, a Plans calendar with highlighted days. Controls are weaker, though. The Send button is icon-only on the phone, Show stays a select, and the tiny mono labels with faint grid lines tax tired eyes.

The To do ledger is excellent for scanning, with a tick well, a dotted leader to who and when, and an amber 'was due' stamp. Phone Home is a huge poster that pushes the box down, though the full-width SEND is clear. Tiny uppercase mono tabs and kickers hurt legibility, 2 Home targets are under 44px, and the Status page is dense and plain.

The poster headlines are striking but cost reading room. Tabs and kickers are tiny uppercase mono, 2 small targets, and To do is plain stacked cards without overdue emphasis. The least improvement in task clarity over today's page.

fixes.suggestion: Keep the pills, the green Add key, the labelled Send and the NOW timeline. Give Ideas the same pills so one kind of filter looks and works one way. Raise the 10-11px mono labels to at least 12px, and make the lit corner visible at normal size.

Keep the labelled Send, the overdue stamps and the Contents dock. Let the tube column collapse on lists to give rows width, and make the Finish setting up strip a single readable line, not three wrapped cells.
Superseded by r20-mut-1. Carry its tidier dock, and keep the select's check mark.
Superseded by r20-mut-3. Take its pills and labelled Send.
Keep the ledger for To do. Shrink the phone poster so the composer sits above the fold, restore a text size of 12px or more on the tabs, and fix the 2 undersized targets.
Superseded by r20-mut-2. Add overdue emphasis to To do and trim the poster size on the phone.

notes: The owner's test is that the change must show across the page content. The two Lit Index entries clear it most clearly: the poster type, the numbered index and the ledger change every page, and the halo stays on the lit word and the tube only. The Grid pair is the most coherent system but reads closer to today, and r20-mut-3 is a thin step on r19-mut-4. The Desk pair is the most authentic CRT but the least changed, and r20-mut-1 is close to a duplicate of r19-mut-1. The weakness of the top pick is loudness, not muddiness.

scores.why: Still the signature, but it is a glare field: 83% green, 17:1 ink, flat card grid, nothing a family would call varied. It is the yardstick for what the owner called too bright and too contrasty.

Biggest visible change across the pages. The condensed poster type, the lit question mark that matches MIND, ruled index heads, and the To do ledger with its rail and amber stamps all show on every page. The bloom and scanline effect is kept on the lit word and the tube only. Weak spots: the Home ledger wraps in a half column, the poster is loud, and the 'editor theme' risk is real.

Same strong editorial system and the same lit MIND, with a grounded cool rail and companion colours with jobs. It loses to its child because To do is still plain stacked rows with a thin 'Edit, complete, or snooze' link, and the question mark is not lit.

The calmest, most systematic page. Banked colours, a lit rail and a tickless lattice hold the whole page together, and the green key plus latched pills make the controls clearer. But the lit corner is almost invisible, only To do got pills, and next to its parent it reads as the same page. The grid floor and rail edge toward sci-fi HUD.

A strong structure, with the best halo-to-calm balance on Home and a wide, legible Plans grid. The grounded neutrals work. But it is busy with lines and lattice, and on To do the Add fold is a dull box sitting next to the filters.

The Desk Terminal glass is the most authentic CRT in the field, and the 56px question has more spark. But the change from r19 is nearly invisible, the setup strip pushes Coming up off the first screen, and the page is one dense dark-teal plate under the glass.

A calm, tidy, grounded desk with a good tube. It is the most conventional app layout of the six, with small type and plates that look alike, and the tonal ground gets a little grey-teal. The least distinct from today in structure.

fixes.suggestion: Keep the lit-mark poster, the ledger, the index heads and the amber stamps. Fix the Home ledger's wrapped titles by giving it full width or dropping the Who column. Use the poster scale only on the Home and page titles, and keep the display face off the Settings row titles.
Keep the poster, the numbered index and the cool rail. Adopt the lit question mark and the ledger from r20-mut-2. Make To do rows a single line rather than stacked cards.

Keep the banked colours, the lit rail and the keyed To do controls. Roll the pills out to the Ideas filters, strengthen the lit corner so it shows at half size, and quiet the grid floor and the rail edge.
Keep the calm lattice and the clear Plans grid. Fold the Add fold into the control row as a key, and reduce line density at the page margins.
Keep the 56px question and the glass. Fix the setup strip's dashed cells and bring Coming up back onto the first screen, for example by making the setup strip a one-line summary.
Keep the tube and the dock track. It needs larger type steps, and open bands so the plates stop repeating. Both of those are in r20-mut-1, so this one is redundant.

notes: All six differ strongly from today across the pages, so none fails the owner's 'nearly identical' test. The three Grid Console and Lit Index lines are the strongest because they combine the owner's favourite elements: fine tracks with stops, a lit question with a real halo, and grounded companion colours on each rail. Desk Terminal is handsome, with the best tube, but it reads more as a modern dashboard with a monitor in it, and its Even Dock change is nearly invisible. The r20 mutants are tiny steps on their parents, so I spread the scores by how well each small step answers a real weakness: the keyed controls do (r20-mut-3), the lit question mark does a little (r20-mut-2), and the equalised dock barely does (r20-mut-1). Lit Index is the only one with a new typographic voice, which the owner would enjoy, but its CRT soul is carried by MIND and the small tube alone.

scores.why: The original glow and CRT soul are intact, but it is the all-green, high-contrast page the owner asked to calm, with little structure or colour variation.
A real green tube with a lit question and chart, slate trays and thin rule lines; grounded and clearly different from today, but it reads as a tidy modern dashboard around one screen.

A bold editorial poster with a huge lit MIND, a rail-coloured index and a small CRT; very different and the glow is real, but the line-art tracks are sparse and the style is far from the period CRT feel.

Fine lit rails, tracks with a NOW lamp and dots, a glowing question in a lit panel, and a different companion hue on each rail; the closest to the Signal Box line art the owner loves, and it keeps the phosphor glow on the question.
The same Desk Terminal with a bigger, hotter question and a setup strip first; a good glass moment, but the equalised dock is barely visible and the strip pushes Coming up off the first screen.

Lit Index with the question mark lit to match MIND and calmer, larger kickers, so the poster is more coherent; the To do ledger hangs from a lit rail, but that is not visible on Home and the change from the parent is small.

Grid Console with a green primary key, pill filters on To do and a lit corner on the first cell; the controls look pressable and the rails and glow stay, though the changes from the parent are small and Ideas is inconsistent.

fixes.suggestion: Keep the rails, the NOW lamp and the keyed controls. Carry the pills and the green key to Ideas and Plans so the control system is consistent, and make the lit corner visible at small size.
The best structure and line art. The parent of r20-mut-3; keep its calm but take the keyed controls from r20-mut-3.

The typographic poster is the boldest new idea. Show the ledger on Home above the fold and use rails that draw the eye through the page the way the Grid Console tracks do; make sure the poster feels like a phosphor tube across every page, not only on Home.
Keep the bolder lit question on the glass. Put Coming up back above the setup strip, or make the strip a single compact line, so the first screen is not pushed down.
Add thin tracks that connect the numbered sections, as the Grid Console tracks do, and keep the huge MIND as the lit centrepiece.

notes: The designs with the most tube in them are the Desk Terminal pair. They set the question, gauge and radar inside scanlined glass with bloom, so the CRT shows up in the content of Home, Status and Ideas and not only the corner. Lit Index has the boldest single lit image, the giant scanlined MIND, but its Ideas and Status heads are quiet editorial type. Grid Console is grounded and calm, with the least phosphor glow of the five. Today's page keeps the halo and the monitor, but there is little else to it. For the final I would put the Desk Terminal first, with Lit Index close behind for how well its poster is lit.

scores.why: The original tube light is all there (halo on the key word, scanlined monitor, glowing lamp), but it stops at the monitor and a few marks, and the rest is flat cards that read as generic dark UI.

The Home question is typed on its own scanlined glass with a block cursor and a LISTENING status line, and Status and Ideas get a gauge and a radar on real tubes, so the green-screen effect is on the page content and not in a corner.

The lit MIND poster has real scanlines and bloom, and the grey-bezel monitor is a convincing 1980s object, but Ideas and Status are plain editorial type with only a thin green rule, so the tube feels like a guest on a calm page.
The cell lattice and teal cast are tasteful and calm, but MIND is only half lit and the faint grid replaces the glow, so the page reads more engineered than phosphor.

It keeps the Desk Terminal's glass, gauge and radar and makes the question bigger with a hotter core. Heavier strokes and layered halo bring back the original lit-word effect, and the docked tubes and open bands keep the page calm around them.

Lighting the question mark makes the poster one lit line with a visible halo, and the ledger and mono kickers add typographic soul, but the light stays on Home and the monitor while other pages go dark and flat.
The lit corner tick and green Add key give small lit accents, and the yellow focus edge is nice, but it is the quietest design for glow and the changes from its parent are barely visible at a glance.

fixes.suggestion: Keep the 56px glass question with the hot core, the LISTENING line and the gauge on the Status tube. Fix the long question clipping at narrow widths by letting it wrap or step down, and let the lit halo reach one more place on content pages (a lit count or key word in a list head) so Plans and To do feel it too.

Keep the lit MIND and question mark as the one big lit line. Carry a small amount of that bloom to the page-head numerals on Ideas and Status so the glow is a system and not a Home poster, and keep the grey-plastic monitor.

The lit corner is the right idea of light as a signal, but it is too faint. Give it the original two-layer halo on the live cell only, and let a lit word in each head echo it so the lattice has something burning on it.
The grid backdrop is calm but cold. Add scanlines and a soft bloom to the lit half of MIND so the green gets back its screen-light character.

notes: The field is three families, each with a parent and a nearly identical child, and half-size cards hide most of the r20 differences. Lit Index is the standout for taste and memorability. Its condensed poster face, lit MIND, mono kickers and per-section coloured rules (green, violet, blue, amber) give a clear mood: a lit index card on a tube. It also brings back the original phosphor halo where it belongs, on the key word and the small tube, with grounded colour elsewhere. Desk Terminal has the most literal CRT feel, with the pixel-font question on the glass, but is boxier and busier. Grid Console is the most systemic and calm, with its NOW rail and UP lamp, and the quietest personality. Today's page keeps the best glow but is the most generic. For the final I want the poster type system and rails, the glass with its pixel question, and the threaded grid with its controls kept as separate ideas worth combining.

scores.why: Cohesive and pleasant, with the best bloom and halo, but generic dark cards with one green and little typographic personality.

The terminal glass with a pixel-font question, a LISTENING line, a chart in the tube and a numbered Contents plate gives a real machine-room character across the page, though it is a little busy and boxy.

The most memorable identity in the field: a huge condensed poster question with MIND lit, mono kickers, per-section coloured rules and hatched kind swatches. It is editorial and CRT together, with a small tube as a trophy.

A lattice with threaded section nodes, a NOW marker with a lit line to it, a horizon-grid UP lamp and quiet companion colours. It is tasteful and systemic, but calmer and closer to a dashboard than a statement.

The same terminal language with a bolder 56px lit question and open bands. It is slightly more confident than its parent, but the change is subtle, and setup-first pushes the machine and Coming up below the fold.

The poster identity is kept and extended: the lit question mark makes one glowing line, and the ledger To do with its rail and amber stamps shows the system working beyond the poster. The larger kickers help the typesetting.

The calm lattice gains a green key, latched pills, a lit corner and a taller composer, which are good control ideas but faint at half size. It stays close to its parent and reads as polish, not a new look.

fixes.suggestion: Keep the lit poster, the mono kickers and the ledger rail. Fix the sparse half-width To do on Home (give it a full row or stop the title wrapping), and tame the heavy poster on the phone so the question does not shout over the composer. Let the section head numerals carry a little more companion colour.

Keep the green key, the latched pills and the threaded NOW rail. Carry the pills to Ideas so the control system is consistent, and make the lit corner visible at half size with a stronger tick. Give the Home question some typographic drama like the poster.

Keep the glass with its lit pixel question and the Listening line. Move Coming up above the setup strip, or collapse the strip to one line, so the machine and the schedule share the first screen. Make the open bands more different from the parent, with a stronger rule or numeral.
Now superseded by r20-mut-2. Its Chat page, with the lit question as a thread header and the timeline rail, is worth lifting whole.

notes: The Lit Index pair gives the best glance, with title, then the one action, then content, and it brings back the original tube light where it belongs, while the Desk Terminal pair gives the best task path with its tube and big Send. The r20 mutants are close to their parents on the phone use card: r20-mut-1 against r19-mut-1 is a heavier question and little else, and r20-mut-3 against r19-mut-4 is a Send label and lit corners. That is against the owner's complaint that the designs look nearly identical. r20-mut-2 spends its changes on real content (the To do ledger, the lit question mark, kickers, chat leaders) and earns the highest score. The cards show only a few controls, so the pill and key work of r20-mut-3 is promising but cannot be seen across pages.

scores.why: Clear flow and a strong focus ring, but 45 of 57 Home targets are under 44px, the question and Send are small, and the page is one green wash with little hierarchy beyond the glow.
Most legible task path on a phone: tube question, big full-width Send, labelled FROM, a real check-marked dropdown, zero small targets; the page is still close to a uniform dark slab at a squint.
The poster question gives a squint-proof title, then composer, then SEND, and the uppercase tabs and arrow chips make a system; only 2 small targets and a bit of poster height cost it.
Boxed composer reads well and the select list is clean, but the icon-only Send beside the mic is easy to miss and the squint is flat and dim, so the glance tells little.
Same sound phone flow as its parent with a hotter, bolder question and Finish setting up first, but the even dock only shows on desktop and on a phone it looks the same as r19-mut-1.

Best glance hierarchy, with the lit poster question leading to the composer and SEND, and the To do ledger with its dated stamps changes real content a family member uses; a small cost is the half-width ledger on Home and 2 small targets.
Send now says Send, To do gets a green Add key and latched pills, so the controls become a more consistent system, but only To do got them and the squint is still dim and flat.

fixes.suggestion: Keep the lit poster, tab bar and ledger; give the ledger the full row width on Home (stack Wishes below) so titles stop wrapping, and bring the two small targets up to 44px.

Keep the green key, latched pills and Send that says Send; extend the pills to Ideas' three selects so the filter pages share one control system, and lift the squinted hierarchy with one lit title line.
Keep the bolder tube question and Finish setting up strip; make the even dock matter by showing it at phone width too, otherwise it is a desktop-only difference.
Its dropdown with a check mark and the big Send are the best control pair; carry them into the Lit Index and add one more lit element below the fold so the squint shows more than the glass.

notes: The six are three families, each with a refinement beside its parent: Desk Terminal (r19-mut-1, r20-mut-1), Lit Index (r19-mut-3, r20-mut-2) and Grid Console (r19-mut-4, r20-mut-3). Within a family the half-size cards are close to identical, so the mutants earn only small score gaps. All three families really do change the page content (headings, lists, controls, figures), unlike a corner wash, and all three pull the green share well under today's 83%. Next to today's page, all are better on the owner's 'more variation' test. The skeptic's worries are the cool tinted grounds (hue 205-236), the grid and rail glow tipping Grid Console toward the Matrix, and the Lit Index poster type being loud when the owner said the page was too contrasty. Controls and ledger rows are the most portable gains.

scores.why: A calm, tidy page, but it is 83% green and reads as one green wash on black, with identical cards on every page; it is what the owner called 'nearly identical' to everything else.
Grounded slate and brass companions and a real tube and gauge column change the content of every page, but the cool tinted ground (hue 236) is close to an editor theme and the dock ends ragged.

Poster-scale condensed white headings and slab rules carry real typographic personality, but they are louder and more contrasty than the owner asked for, the To do rows are plain, and the near-black ground goes cold.

Keeps the most original CRT light (lit rails, gauge, timeline with a glowing NOW), but the rails and grid glow on every page come close to the Matrix, and Status turns into a field of identical cells.
The best-balanced of the field: wider lists beside the tube, open bands that quiet the page and a heavier question on the glass. Still a tinted cool ground, and its step over r19-mut-1 is slight.

The ledger on To do (tick wells, leader dots, amber stamp) and the 13.6px kickers are real typesetting gains across pages. It is still the cold, loud-headline family, and a half-width ledger on Home wraps.

Adds what the other Grid Console lacked: a visible green key, pill filters and a taller composer. The lit corner is nearly invisible at half size, Ideas is left inconsistent, and the grid-glow Matrix risk remains.

fixes.suggestion: Keep the tube and gauge column and the open bands. Warm the slate ground a few degrees toward neutral so it does not read as an editor theme, and bring back one lit element per list so Status does not go flat.

Keep the green key, the latched pills and the NOW timeline. Give the lit corner a stronger halo, put the pills on Ideas too, and cut the background grid and rail glow to just the section heads so it stays clear of the Matrix.
Keep the ledger and the kicker scale. Soften the white poster headings one step toward the warm ink, and let the ledger take the full width on Home.
The timeline and the gauge are the idea to lift out. Drop the cell-per-item Status and the all-over grid lines.
The poster type has presence. Use it for the page title only, not for every row title, and put colour in the body, not just the rules.
